brief.headline: Cut the price on our top two bottles and caps by 19.6% and 11.1% to match Mars Plastics, saving us ₹16.09 L a year.

priceAsk.summary: Bring the HDPE 30 ML bottle down from ₹1.65/NOS to ₹1.38/NOS (Mars Plastics' price) and the PP 28 mm cap down from ₹0.90/NOS to ₹0.81/NOS (also Mars).
priceAsk.target: ₹16.09 L annual saving by matching the best prices we already pay
priceAsk.basis: We pay Mars Plastics ₹1.38/NOS for the same 30 ML bottle (Premier charges ₹1.65, a 19.6% gap costing us ₹11.74 L/year) and ₹0.81/NOS for the same cap (Premier charges ₹0.90, an 11.1% gap costing us ₹4.23 L/year). The open-market asking price for the 28 mm cap sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, so even ₹0.81 is competitive and ₹0.65–0.80 is reachable at higher volume.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 30 days.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹10.63 L cash freed up for us

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, debt or how tight their cash is. Our ₹1.29 Cr annual spend gives us a seat at the table, but without their numbers we can't gauge how hard to push on price alone. That makes lining up a strong second source — Manjushree Technopack (India's largest rigid-plastic converter, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score 65/100) or a listed player like Mold-Tek — the top priority to keep leverage real.

evidence.point: We pay ₹16.09 L more per year than the lowest prices we already get for the same rigid-plastic items.
The HDPE 30 ML bottle costs us ₹1.65/NOS from Premier but only ₹1.38/NOS from Mars Plastics — a 19.6% gap.
That single bottle gap alone costs us ₹11.74 L a year in extra spend.
The PP 28 mm induction-wad cap costs us ₹0.90/NOS from Premier versus ₹0.81/NOS from Mars — an 11.1% gap worth ₹4.23 L/year.
Open-market asking prices for the 28 mm cap run ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, so our ₹0.90 is market-fair but there's room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume.
Shortening payment terms from 45 days to 30 days frees up ₹10.63 L of our cash.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score 65/100), makes pharma bottles, caps and preforms — the strongest second-source candidate we have.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging; strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: IVL Dhunseri Petrochem Industries Private Limited (marketBackups lead)
alternates.why: A manufacturer lead in India-East to qualify (verify capability and price before issuing RFQ) — potential upstream source for resin or preforms.

risks: Premier's financials aren't public, so we can't tell if a hard price squeeze might tip them into trouble or if they have room to absorb the cut — keep the tone firm but not punitive.
If they walk, we need Manjushree or Mold-Tek qualified and priced before the next PO cycle — start that parallel RFQ now.
The 30 ML bottle and 28 mm cap together drive ₹16.09 L of the gap; if they only move on one SKU, the saving shrinks fast — insist both items move to Mars-level pricing.

The market-ask data shows the 28 mm cap can drop further (₹0.65–0.80 at volume), so if they only come down to ₹0.81 and stop, we may be leaving money on the table — probe for a volume-tier discount below ₹0.81.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're paying you ₹1.65 for the 30 ML bottle and ₹0.90 for the 28 mm cap, but Mars Plastics gives us ₹1.38 and ₹0.81 for the same items — that's costing us ₹16 lakh a year, and we need those gaps closed.
